The platoon commander and the first lieutenant, Spanish first lieutenant, what is usually the situation, was standing halfway above the hatch of his APC - the rest was under -- under armour - and was shot almost at the same place on the road of Tito Bridge where -- where we were hit from the west side as we discussed before. He was hit by a direct -- a direct shot and brought to the east, and I think that he died there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, in the report you wrote -- you said that the shot was fired from the blue glass building, the school, and the old bank. So -- I believe that's what it says. "The shots were fired from the blue glass building, the school, and the old bank, west side, HVO held." Could you tell us why you wrote that, what's the basis of that statement and whether there was any sort of ability to conduct a formal forensic investigation of the incident?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, the investigations officially from the Spanish government and a lot of other organisations was done later on. This is based on our own interpretation as we did, and I explained to you previously as we did with our own vehicle. This was also the report at the end of the day, so very fresh, by our own expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So just to be clear, this wasn't the result of a scientific investigation. It's just your own opinion based on --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- what you saw. Okay. Now, recalling that this incident occurred while the convoy was in the process of delivering medicines to the east side hospital, and recalling that that's an issue that you were working on in general, how did this incident, this sniper incident, affect then your ability to arrange further supplies of medicines and doctors to go into East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Firstly it frustrated UNPROFOR and especially the Spanish Battalion, and as a result of that they stopped that kind of escort, that kind of transport, I have to say. Finally, because the situation was really very bad in the war hospital, we did it ourselves twice. We did it in our small jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. One last point on this to clarify -- actually, two points. The blue glass building that's referred to in this memo, is that the building that's in the photograph that you looked at earlier?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, also in this memo you referenced shots, that is more than one shot, has been fired from different locations, and I wanted to ask you just to clarify, if you can, what that's about. That was Exhibit 2731 again, sorry.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Let me read it for a moment, please. Yeah. That means that there was more than one shot from -- from the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. The next exhibit is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Colonel, if you could clarify one thing. In this document 2731, you indicate that the shots came from the blue building, in other words, the building that we saw in the picture. And you also note in this document that it was a convoy carrying medication from the west, from the hospital located in the western part, to the hospital located in the eastern part, and that the convoy transporting that medication was taking the Tito Bridge, travel along the Tito Bridge. And so if I understood you correctly this convoy was travelling from the west to the east. Is that the itinerary that you indicate in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's always a shame we don't have maps before us. I've already said that in the past. We know, because we have already looked at pictures, and we've heard testimony, we've looked at depositions, we know that the Spanish lieutenant was shot at by shots coming from his left, from his left. So with regard to the Tito Bridge, the blue building, is the Blue Building located on the left of the Tito Bridge when you are coming from Mostar west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The blue bank building, when you come from the west side, is situated on the right of the Tito Bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, sir, that it's -- it's -- maybe it is a misunderstanding, but the only thing what happens probably is a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which means that you don't really know more about this. You don't know whether the building was on the left or the right of the Tito Bridge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, from -- from -- it depends from which position you want to know it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll come back to that later. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Sometimes I think -- maps certainly would be useful. Sometimes I think it's a fatality of the time constraints. I'll do my best to clarify that during the witness's direct examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: For now, however, let me move on, Colonel, to the next exhibit, which is 2756. Is this one of your reports dated 14th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 of this report, there's a reference to information received from three different sources about Muslim families being expelled by HVO soldiers from their homes in the south-east quarter. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Expulsions from the quarter Dum and Vatikana. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then finally a reference to HVO stickers being placed on the doors of those apartments after the expulsions occur. At this point in time, which is the 14th of June, I'd like you -- you've talked about this issue of expulsions already. Are you able to comment on the extent of this practice, whether it's increasing, decreasing, the level of organisation or lack of organisation as you saw it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: This was mid-June. It was definitely increasing at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If you would turn to Exhibit 2735, which requires you to go backwards. I want to ask you whether you recognise that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I do. It is a page out my -- from my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you just tell the Trial Chamber, please, about the various markings in it, some of which had Bosnian names. Other parts are written in Dutch, and other parts have a little bit of English. Perhaps you could decipher it all for us.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Actually, if -- I take that back, and let me try to walk you through a couple of sections of it sort of just to move things along. You say this is from your notebook.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the writings there of the Bosnian names, Rahimic Mustafa in the middle, did you write that or did someone else write that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No. That is the handwriting of our interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did these names come to you, why was she writing there?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: This is information we got from the street, and as soon as someone came with a message to our vehicle or to one of our team members, then we asked our interpreter to translate it, and especially names were then immediately written by her.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Because we were not able to -- to understand that in the -- especially the names, not in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this was a source of information you're getting on the street?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In West Mostar.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, up in the top left corner there appear the words "Vatikana and Dum"?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We just referenced those in the report, that's Exhibit 2756, a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, is the information that you're picking up here being reflected then in the report that you subsequently prepared?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then just a couple of other parts here down toward the bottom it says "1400 hours on Saturday, 12/6/93 by HVO soldiers expelled". Again is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then up in the middle. It's written smaller in the right: "Now occupied by HVO soldiers." Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So that's just a reflection of the information that you were being given at that time from someone on the street; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How much credit would you give that information standing alone?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Standing alone it could be a rumour, but with verifying it and confirming this by other sources it -- the picture became -- became more -- more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you would turn to the next exhibit, 2744.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, and with your permission and the assistance the usher, perhaps I could hand the original of this exhibit to the witness that was previously discussed by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Colonel, there has been discussion about the current condition of this exhibit and the passage of time. Do you recognise this -- this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us about this, how you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It's a paper we received from someone with the names, but it's very hard to read. Under Dum in typewriting letters you find five names of HVO personnel. And the rest is my handwriting adding in the sixth one, and that refers also to my -- to my note you saw in the previous question. A sixth name was added by myself to this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the handwriting that's on the right-hand side, list of HVO soldiers, whose handwriting is that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And just for the record at the bottom right where it says, "Attachment," is that the notation of the investigator when you turned this over?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, was this another source then about the information about the expulsion of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then is this information reflected in your report of the 14th of June, which is Exhibit 2756?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. One last question on that one -- I take that back. We can move on to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Colonel, on the document that you have before you, it's a sheet of paper torn, we can see where it was torn, someone handed this paper to you, someone in the street? Is that how things occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the street, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when he handed this to you, what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that is what I -- what I wrote here myself by hand, that the five soldiers were recognised expelling Muslims on that date at that time.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes, but this unknown individual who handed the paper to you, he hands to you a paper on which five names are typed, among which Stela, the first name, when he hands this paper to you does he stay that this is a list of those who are -- who were at the time expelling or evicting Muslims, or did he just hand this paper to you and leave? Did you have an actual conversation with this individual and with the interpreter present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, because as a result of that conversation I made this note on the paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So does this mean that this unknown individual had himself or else somewhere else had typed a list of individuals whom he was denouncing, in fact? By handing you this document and dealing you they things he was denouncing these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And why did you add the six the name, Viktor Markovic? Why did you add the sixth name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because at the same -- in the same conversation that was added. So the list was not complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So it was that individual who told you that there was also among those people Viktor Markovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the individual who handed this list to you, I assume he was wearing civilian clothing, or was he wearing military clothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer the -- that question. I don't -- I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But was he a Croat or a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was handed over on the west bank. That is for sure. On the west bank, not on the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but it could have been a Croat or a Bosnian. It could have been anyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For sure, sir, but unfortunately I can't tell you his -- his ethnic background, and I even don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. And on the basis of this document, you drafted a report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. We mentioned it, yeah. In the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question, but I think my colleague will then have a question for you. I noted that your interpreter was of Muslim origin. Was it not taking a risk for international civil servants to hire as interpreters representatives of one faction, one party? Is there not a risk of various forms of manipulation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had a pool of interpreters in Siroki Brijeg, and we had Croats as well. And of course there was always a risk, sure. But -- but let me explain. They were working, let's say, under more or less our protection, and they had official papers from ECMM, also translated in Bosnian, Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But I note somewhat oddly, curiously, that your interpreter takes you to the place where people were allegedly expelled. So you are brought to one might say the place where the crime was committed. You're taken to an apartment. We saw pictures, an apartment that allegedly was visited. Some larceny was committed given the state that we see, the fact that shots were fired, and by coincidence it's your interpreter who takes you to the place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in this particular case we -- I have to explain how it worked. We went home before darkness, as I said before, and in the morning, before we started the trip, the first thing we did was picking her up from their home place, and what happened sometimes is that she gave us information, because people went to her place and -- and came with -- with messages. In this particular case, talking about the pictures, I mean, not -- not this piece of paper but referring to -- to the pictures I took at that specific address, that was by -- by her information. That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be of assistance. You may wish to ask the gentleman, because on page 2 on his witness statement he deliberately says, "We deliberately had hired a Muslim interpreter because we were afraid that the Bosnian Croat interpreters would brief the Bosnian Croat leaders about us." So here is somewhat of a direct contradiction of what he indicated earlier, because here he says, "we deliberately hired a Muslim ... " So I think it's in line with your questions, Mr. President. You may wish to explore that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Counsel for Defence here is observing, is noting something. You said that you deliberately had hired a Muslim interpreter to make sure that the interpreter would not brief the Bosnian Croat leaders on what you were doing, but wasn't there a risk that she could brief the ABiH on what you were doing? There is a risk on both sides. And was this risk correctly assessed by your organisation and yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Definitely, sir, because we know how intel works, and we had Croat interpreters, as I said, in Siroki Brijeg. One of the reasons, and we were lucky to do so and allowed to do so, was to make our own choice not using them in Siroki Brijeg for going downtown Mostar exactly for that reason, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but maybe I'm going to ask a silly question, but why didn't you hire Serbian interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the most important reason probably is that she was studying English. So that was the first very important reason to do so. And she was living in -- in, let's say, in a very, for us, convenient place for doing business and picking her up in the morning. So there were a lot of practical things to go for her as well. And at the moment that we did, we were convinced she was not involved in any system involved. Let me say it that way. So we trust her at that moment very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, I would like to stop for a moment and draw your attention, if need be, on the content of this slip of paper where there are names, names of HVO soldiers who would allegedly have evicted Muslim people. I find it very hard to understand and to accept that someone would hand you over a slip of paper like that and that you would turn it over to the Prosecutor. If this document is admitted as an exhibit, there are great consequences that may derive from it. So this is my question: Did your team have any legal or police competence or competence in terms of intelligence gathering so that you were able to cross a number of information to make sure that this document was really strong enough to be shown to the Prosecutor? I would really like to be assured -- reassured about this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we hadn't in our organisation such an intel specialist, but this came from my personal -- my personal notes and documents I still had when I returned, and I showed that to the Prosecutor in January 2002 -- or, let's say, in the preparation phase for my first testimony, and it was up to them to accept it, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had a number of questions asked about this document, but Mr. Stringer, you can resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, on this note and the others, or the other one that you mentioned, you've described the situation with people coming up to you in the street with information. Isn't it possible that they were manufacturing evidence and that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. It calls for speculation, Your Honour. It calls for speculation. "Isn't it possible?" A lot of things, possible. What is fact? That's what we are dealing with here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can restate the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you consider whether the information being provided was false or that you were attempting -- others were attempting to mislead you about the situation on expulsion of Muslims in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not at that moment when we received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Over time did information continue to come in from other sources about this activity?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you have any doubts about whether in fact that was happening during this period of time in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is P 2782. This is one of your reports, is it not, from the 15th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Bottom of page 1 there's a reference to a meeting. You've got a list of materials needed from the east side hospital. And then turning the page, I want to ask you about two things there. Moving down a few lines there's a reference to an HVO offer. "The HVO offered to take care of all the wounded people, Muslims or Croats, including people from the east side." And then it continues: "We asked the SpaBat commander to provide transport of medicines from the west hospital to the east one, but we've been told that they need, before providing the transport, an agreement signed by both parts." The first question is could you comment on the likelihood or the possibility of, in fact, moving all of the people in the east side hospital to the west side and taking advantage of this offer that was extended by the Croats on the west side? Did that happen? If not --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, why not?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It didn't happen, because finally there was no agreement by both parties, and also the Spanish Battalion at that very moment was not very happy to -- to provide the -- the escort after the incident with the lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was it feasible to think that all of the patients on the east side could have been moved out to the west side?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I think it was of not feasible at that moment because they -- they were also very afraid for their -- for their existence, actually, at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was the reason why they were so concerned or afraid about that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Because the overall situation was that bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know if the incident involving the lieutenant who was killed on the APC would have affected or did affect the Spanish Battalion's willingness to participate?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Definitely, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then moving to the next page, paragraph 6, under the assessment: "At present the transport of wounded people from the east side to the west is totally impossible due to the snipers." Was that your assessment at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again there's another reference to ethnic cleansing on the west side, a Muslim. Was that continuing to take place based on your information?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is P 2806. Colonel, this is -- well, is this one of your M2 reports prepared by you and your colleague Mr. Amatriain?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. There is reference in this report to a couple of meetings that you had on this day, 16th of June, and I'd like to ask you to talk about those. Did you have a meeting with Mr. Pusic and Mr. Coric on this day, the 16th of June?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And is that meeting -- is that meeting indicated here that -- the topics that were raised during that meeting, looking at the top of page 2?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. We were talking about a visit to the Heliodrom, I think. Let me check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I direct you to the top of page 2.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. The Heliodrom, and of course what was going on in -- in the western part concerning expelling of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And after this meeting with Messrs. Pusic and Coric, then, did you have a separate meeting with Defence Minister Stojic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you tell us about the first meeting, specifically what would have been the issues you would have raised or did raise with Pusic and Coric, and what responses they gave to the issues that you had raised with them?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Bottom line of that discussion was that -- that they were not able to give answers on our questions, the same questions we had for the commander over there as I told you before, and that they said that the people over there are not accused yet because all the cases are under investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, is this a reference to the people in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the specific issues you raised in regard to the Heliodrom about the situation out there with them?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we were asking why they were there, what were the -- the charges against these people, for how long. And then we discussed, of course, the situation, the situation in the camp itself, so the bad circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And what was the response regarding this issue of their being held there and not knowing why they were held?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, that was -- that was used frequently. "We don't have" -- "We are not able to give you that answer because it's a war situation," and that was the justification, more or less, for not giving answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you said you also raised the issue of Muslim expulsions from West Mostar. What was the -- well, let me ask you, what was the response with regard to that issue? What did they say?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That it didn't happen, and if it happened, then it was done by -- by people they didn't had under control, criminals or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was that response acceptable to you, or was it one that you could accept based on what you -- you were observing and learning about in Mostar at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We had to accept these kind of answers, but for -- for ourselves, it was, of course, not acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And why do you say that? Why was it not acceptable?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Because I -- we believed, the team believed, that it was organised and that there was a plan to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, moving down the second page there's reference now to the meeting you had with Mr. Stojic on the same day. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again just so we know, where did these meetings take place?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: In his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what about Messrs. Pusic and Coric? Where did that meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: In his office as well, the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Whose office?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: The office of, I suppose -- well, that's hard to recall. I don't know if it was the office of Mr. Coric or Mr. Pusic, but they were both at the same meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And this is in the ministry building?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, what were the issues that you raised with Mr. Stojic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Actually, the same issues we raised in the previous meeting with Mr. Coric and Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That being the Heliodrom and then also expulsion or evictions?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, there's a reference here. What was Mr. Stojic's response regarding the 504 prisoners in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, it's in this report. It was more or less the same statement that they were still not accused but under investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And what was -- what did he say about the issue of expulsions of Muslim civilians from West Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: More or less the same answer: "We are not involved in it. When it happened, then it was done by criminals."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you also raise with Mr. Stojic the issue of the shooting of the Spanish Battalion lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We did, because we -- we asked both sides to -- to give us the outcome of their investigation upon the murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Stojic's response or comment on that issue?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojic in that meeting, and that's why you can read it here in the report, answered that -- that the shooting was not coming from the west side and the blue -- the blue bank building, because he had all snipers under control, also in the gymnasium. That was his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He said he had all snipers under full control?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In which locations?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: The blue bank building, as we call it, and the gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The blue bank building being the structure that you identified in the photograph earlier?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, Prosecutor asked you a question but he hadn't ask the question I would have asked myself. During your conversation with Mr. Stojic, according to your report it seems that what you were talking about the death of the Spanish officer, Mr. Stojic said that it was the ABiH who committed this crime, but it seems that added -- when you read the sentence that the HVO did not shoot at that time, and in English you write: "[In English] And all snipers were under full control," so Mr. Stojic would have told you that all snipers were under full control in the gymnasium and in the blue bank building. So Mr. Stojic himself told you that the snipers located in these two buildings were under HVO control? He said that himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. This is not my text. It is the text I noted or we noted after that conversation. So that is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So what you're writing are Mr. Stojic's words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm going to move to Exhibit 2898, if I may. Colonel, very briefly on this one. Again, is this one of your reports, that is you and Mr. Amatriain, of the 22nd of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And the bottom of the first page there's a reference to an attempt to meet with Mr. Stojic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And now did you succeed to meet with him that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: They propose that you meet instead with Mr. Bosic. You refuse. I'm just wondering if you recall or if you can shed light on why you would have rejected a proposal to meet with Mr. Bosic instead of Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, sometimes it happened at that Mr. Stojic was not available and we talked to Mr. Bosic, but in this specific case, I suppose, because now -- now it's hard to recall, of course, but the only reason could be is that he promised us answers on specific important things we wanted to hear from himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: There's a reference here to information from the Spanish Battalion commander that the Donja Mahala quarter has run out of food completely, and as there are a lot of refugees and displaced people, they are asking for visits from organisational -- international organisations and assistance. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the refugees and displaced people, do you know, if you know, who were they, where were they, and where had they come from in general?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's very hard --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: -- to answer. I can't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And that was a bad question. Is this -- is there any connection between this reference and then people who were being evicted from West Mostar, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we -- what I can say at this moment only is that we had that information from other sources as well. This was not new for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Talking about that specific area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. The next exhibit is 2923.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, are we going to go to 20 minutes past the hour? I wasn't sure what time the break would be coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Colonel, do you have Exhibit 2923 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And again, is this one the reports that you prepared, the M2 team, you and Jesus Amatriain?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of page 2 under the section of "Other subjects," and the last line it begins a reference to Mr. Bagaric and the HVO hospital on the west side. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: He was at that time the -- let's say chef de clinic, chief of the west bank hospital organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Is he a person that you had dealings with on these issues of exchange of doctors and supply of medicines?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, in this report there's a reference -- or he's talking about an exchange of doctors that would require HVO doctors from other regions up towards Central Bosnia to be -- have freedom of movement. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then there's also, just moving down a line, a reference of his suggestion to open the old hospital of Mostar on the west side near the front line and use it as a war hospital for everybody. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you just briefly comment on those two points? How feasible was it to achieve an exchange of doctors involving not only those in Mostar but those who are in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Talking about the exchange of doctors, it was more or less the end of our proposal because this was not feasible. So the local situation was linked by him to another situation outside our area where the Croat position was a bad one. And talking about the war hospital in the confrontation zone, of course a show-stopper. It didn't work at that time in that situation, under that kind of dangerous circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Show-stopper, meaning not possible?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again why was it not possible to open up this old war hospital?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if that was possible, but he definitely should not have the possibility to get all the patients there, talking about unsecure transport, for instance. And by the way, the situation in the -- in the confrontation line at that time was too dangerous anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And the location of this old hospital was close to the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then moving down to the bottom of the page there is a reference to the Old Bridge. Information came to you from Mr. Bilic who was on the east side, and I'd just like you to comment on the condition of the Old Bridge as of that time from what you recall, and if you call this issue of a broken water tube that was dropping water on the foundation.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, what I remember is that at that time talking about -- that was the end of June, more or less, yeah. It became more worse than it was before. So the -- the Old Bridge was heavily damaged at that time already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then moving to the next page. Towards the end of your report: "We think the HVO is not willing to deal with humanitarian aid for the east bank." Why did you say that at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, for the same reasons I just explained you. Coming with such a kind of proposal means that you are not really willing to solve the problem on the local -- on the local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see -- did you see any tangible steps taken on the HVO side to achieve some way to alleviate the situation for civilians in East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. The next exhibit is 2941. And is this one of your reports again, dated 25th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. And turning to the second page, at the bottom,, although it may be that the Trial Chamber has heard enough about notes, I'm going to introduce the subject of one more of them. Do you recall receiving a note from a child when you were in West Mostar about this time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Then if you could turn to Exhibit 2935. Tell us whether you recognise that's the note.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Sorry, can you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: 2935, yes. It's back.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. The Official Note is the last one in the Serbo-Croatian language, of course. It starts with, "Help me."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The third page of this?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That was received by you.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And who gave that to you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That was the child we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What part of Mostar were you in when this happened? Your report is 2941, if you want to go back and refer to that.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's hard to say, but maybe in the report it makes clear where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Where we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. It indicates at the bottom you were arranging for the transport of a -- of someone else.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in the course of that this note came to you. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could just briefly tell us, then, what -- after you received this note what -- what did you do about it? Again, it's an another source, I suppose, like the others.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. When we received this, we went to the spot to check if -- if that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what did you -- what, if anything, were you able to find out?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It was -- we were not able at that moment to find exactly the location, but in the vicinity of where it happened, let's say in that neighbourhood, we saw soldiers putting piece of papers on the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me back up a little bit. I don't think I've asked you enough questions about how it led to that. The note itself, what can you give us -- we have the note indicating: "Help me. Yesterday evening a crime was committed there against Alikalfic family, husband and wife, Muslims, their house was mined and they burnt to death in the fire." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, that's the note that you received. Then -- and the date of the note, just for the record?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: 24th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: 24th of June. And this then is again referred to in your report of 25 June. So then you went to this area, as you say, and what did you find when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: As I said, we were not able to find exactly the place where it happened, but in that area we saw soldiers putting papers on -- on the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What kind of papers?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That were announcements about the family. We found out later because our interpreter went out to translate the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: And we found out that it was the same family was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In these notices or papers that were being posted to the trees?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Did you speak to any of the HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving down just a few lines, there's a reference here, you say: "We saw one HV, that is HV car going to Mostar." I'd just like to ask you briefly to comment on that issue whether at this time and other times, you observed HV, that is Croatian army, military personnel in your area of responsibility or elsewhere in Western Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Sometimes we -- we saw them in the Mostar area, but at that time not that often.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Toward the bottom of the page, then, you make a reference here to: "During the last days we've been warned that the HVO is doing a lot of atrocities, raping, burning people in their houses, et cetera. We cannot confirm any case, but we have seen some things related to the events and the sources are completely different." So I wonder if you can just tell the Trial Chamber what source -- what were the sources, if you recall? What was the information that was coming in that was related to these actions?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we normally had information by the intel officer of the Spanish Battalion. We had at that time still contact with the UN military observers, and of course our -- our two teams gave information. So besides that what we heard in the street from different people, I mean, we tried to verify these things as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. The next exhibit is P 3 --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Sorry, maybe -- maybe let me explain why -- why the intel officer of the Spanish battalion was so important. You have to understand that the Spanish Battalion was deployed on company-size level within Mostar. So there came a lot of information via the companies to the battalion, and they made their analysis of the situation. So we are talking about, in the military sense, HumInt was used to produce a picture at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: HumInt being human intelligence?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, human intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just so we know roughly, if you recall the size of a company in the Spanish Battalion at that time. How many individuals are we talking?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: About hundred fifty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 3007. Now, in this -- well, I should ask you, do you recognise this report, Colonel, as one of the ones that you and your colleague prepared?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It is one of our reports, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And this is dated the 29th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. So just sort of setting the stage. This is just prior to, then, an event that we'll talk about probably after the break, which is the ABiH offensive on the northern barracks that occurred on the early morning of the 30th.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So that's where we are in time. You had a conversation here, it's referenced on the middle of page 2, conversation with an individual named Puljic, and I wanted to ask you first of all who was Mr. Puljic? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic was the Chief of Staff at the HVO headquarters in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And actually, during the course of this conversation did you learn that he had a new job or a --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, he told us. Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: He became commander, what normally means a promotion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I don't -- we don't need to go into the details of the whole conversation, but I wanted to ask you, turning to the third page, actually, while there was talk of re-establishing the joint commission, that's on the second page, and then the next page again you're raising this issue about an exchange of doctors, and he indicated that there were pressures on the HVO to avoid agreements, and I want to ask you about that. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No. Can you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sure. If you would turn to page 3.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Moving down about 10 lines. "When we asked him about the exchange of doctors with the east side, he liked the idea, but he told us that some paramilitary organisations still exist in the community of Herceg-Bosna, and they are putting a lot of pressure on the HVO to avoid any agreement with the armija." Right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just taking that, then, and going to the next page, and then we can just talk about all of it. There's a comment here. Again, this is your view under "Assessment," a reference to paramilitary organisations inside or next to the HVO, extremists, nationalists, full of criminals. You go on and you actually mention then by name three individuals, a Tuta, an Andabak, and a Juka. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: "... We had confirmed their high level in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." Those three names, what can you recall now about Tuta, Andabak, Juka, those individuals and your observations of them during the time that you were in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At that time we considered these people not to be a -- member of a paramilitary organisation, but we considered them as a part of the HVO structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Had you met -- well, let's take Tuta first. Had you met him personally or seen him during the course of your travels from Mostar to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I have seen him. I never spoke to him. I saw him several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know where he had an office?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: From our information he had an office at the MOD of HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's what you were informed?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were never there personally?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We never saw him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then Mr. Andabak. Did you ever have any -- up until this date, the 29th, did you have any had you ever met him or seen him?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes, we once met him in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then finally Mr. Juka. Do you recall who that's a reference to?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we -- we were witnessing that he with his group of soldiers sometimes intimidated the -- the -- our joint commission members, the fixed members, especially in this case he was against Colonel Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Intimidating joint commission members. This is the joint commission that you testified about earlier?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you ever present at any joint commission meetings when Mr. Juka Prazina came?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we did. On the west bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: On the west bank.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: As a result of that the next one, and we talked about that prior, was done on the east bank, because we had to transport -- or we UNPROFOR had to secure, to transport the people from the east bank due to this kind of intimidation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe what kind of intimidation of Colonel Pasalic did you see at the time of the joint commission meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Shooting and shouting phrases that made them very tense and unsecure, gave them an unsecure feeling.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see the efforts on the part of other HVO units to control him or to prevent him from getting access to the joint commission?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, UNPROFOR did, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What about the HVO itself?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't have the impression that that was done by HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you say here that initially you indicate that: "We had confirmed their high level in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the HVO." Did you have information that was provided to you, available to you in terms of what was believed to be the hierarchy and the organisational structure within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. We from the beginning intel information from the Spanish Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you to turn to Exhibit 10025. That's 10025. This is one of the ones, Counsel, that was added.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I haven't wanted to interrupt even though we've now had a very long period of essentially multiple-level hearsay and speculation from this witness on a variety of subjects, but am I to understand that Mr. Stringer now is going to have this witness testify about the structure of the HVO based upon intel that he got from the Spanish Battalion, and he's going to be asked to examine a document that he got from this source and give some kind of expert opinion about that, and then make deductions about who was in the upper echelons of the HVO? Because if that is the case, I object strongly. We've had other evidence on this subject, and this witness simply is not competent to provide this sort of opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I wish to join in on that objection. I was waiting, but I was beat for once to the button, but I do object strongly about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have a document, an organisational chart. We've already seen it. It has been challenged. The witness -- one of the witness's mandates was to make reports on what was going on in Mostar, and so the Prosecution can ask him about his point of view, whether he believes that the documents are -- relate to the situation. The Trial Chamber will then draw conclusions on the basis of the many elements that we will have before us, an addition of various pieces of evidence. So please be quick in asking your question because we will take a break in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Colonel, yes, the document that's in front of you, P 10025, do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was that a -- well, tell us what it is. If you could tell the Trial Chamber specifically what this is about?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. This is an updated document dated the 22nd of July, as you see what depicts the structure of the military organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And was this document available to you? Did you have it at the time of your presence in Mostar? In fact, we're talking about a day here that's one week after the date of this, so the 29th of July, 1993. Was this information in your hand at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. It already existed there. That's why I said that this is updated to that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you would just -- counting, if you would just turn -- there are a number of charts here I'm not going to ask you to comment on. If you would just turn to the eighth page of this, because I don't intend to get into a detailed discussion of the HVO structure. The eighth page by my count at the bottom C-4-A. First of all, do you know who made this, how this information was put together?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: This -- this was updated by the intel section of the Spanish Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the eighth page, which I think is the eighth page, there's a box on the left, SPF, and underneath that indicated "Commander M. Naletilic, Tuta." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And next to that there is a reference to Juka and Andabak as commands in their own right at a subordinate level?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So my question now, getting back to your report, is whether this information that's reflected in the Exhibit 10025, whether that's information that you used in making your own characterisations of the relative levels of Juka, Tuta, and Andabak within the HVO organisation.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, this is one of the sources as I explained to you before, but we had also our own observations and other sources to come to a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can leave it there for the break if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us take a break, 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar. Please go back in private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Let's bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed and, Mr. Stringer, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Colonel, just before the break we were looking at your report of 29 July 1993, and we finished that. So that brings us to the 30th of July -- I'm sorry, June, 30th of June 1993, and I'd like to take you to an exhibit which has already been received in evidence, Mr. President. It's Exhibit P 3025. 3025. This would be an ECMM report dated the 30th of June. Do you have that? 3025.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: On the 30th of June do you recall that there was an offensive launched by the ABiH directed against the HVO at a place called the northern barracks?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this is the report made on that day by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your report of 30 June. Now, turning to page 2. We're going to get to this in a minute. You had a number of meetings on that day, the last of which was a meeting or an encounter indicated there with a Mr. Ivan Andabak, commander special unit, HVO. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll talk about that in just a moment, but perhaps if you could skip down and just to perhaps bring you back to where you were when you learned of the ABiH attack that had happened and how that affected your -- your activities pretty much from that point forward. So where were you when you heard about this? I can direct you to page 2, middle of the page. There's a reference to a meeting.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. We went -- by the way, my Spanish colleague was not a member at that time. He was on leave. So the chief of the coordination centre, Mr. Nissen, was the second one. We had a programme also for that day, and we went to -- to the western hospital, the hospital on the west bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And about three-quarters of the way down page 2, it says: "After visiting the HVO hospital, we got the next HVO statement by the military doctor in charge."

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Then we heard for the first time about the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So he gave you sort of a briefing --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- about the events. All right. Now, after you -- well, this event, if you could speak in general terms because here we are the end of June and you were still going to be remaining in this area for almost another two months. Can you describe in general terms how that event changed the situation on the ground, how it affected your ability to move and to gather information as you had before?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. It changed the situation in that respect that -- that it relieved for a moment the situation on the east bank, and we strongly believed at that moment that -- that HVO, the west -- the west side was surprised by this attack. But as consequence of that, they closed the road for us, and we were not able to enter Mostar downtown for more than four weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And as you indicated before, sort of your procedure was to go into Mostar from Siroki Brijeg, and then from West Mostar into East Mostar.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So again, after this development and the closure, were you able to enter either West or East Mostar for that one-month period?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not at all any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, on the third page of this exhibit, which is 3025, after the briefing that you received there's a reference then your having -- "After visiting the hospital we met the family of our Mostar interpreter, and after some time we were warned and ordered to leave Mostar immediately by the special unit of Andabak, HVO, who was at that moment in charge. The unit was preparing an operation in that quarter of Mostar and we had the strong feeling everything had to do which" -- perhaps that's "with"?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: With, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Intimidation, threatening and maybe expelling of Muslim people from that part. So if you could, just briefly, tell the Trial Chamber about that incident and you were encounter with Commander Andabak.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I remember that Mr. Nissen wanted to talk -- well, we were in -- it was the end of the afternoon, and we were at the time to bring back our interpreter. Mr. Nissen wanted to talk to her parents as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me just jump in there. When you say to bring back your interpreter, you mean -- where were you going to take her?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: To her home place. Sorry. To her home place. During the conversation we heard a lot of -- of noise outside, and we saw through the window soldiers deploying, actually, and the people get -- got very excited at that moment, and our interpreter said, "Please leave -- leave the flat as soon as possible, the apartment as soon as possible," and we did. And the moment we left the apartment, walking to our vehicle we -- we met Mr. Andabak, who was very surprised to see us, and who was very angry, actually, directing us to go back to Siroki Brijeg immediately. That was the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was he accompanied by others? Was he with other people?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, at -- at -- what we saw, actually, that he was playing the role of commander of that group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you estimate how many soldiers were present with him?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not the total, but what we counted was at least 15, 1-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And how were the soldiers dressed? Were they in uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: They were in uniform, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Uniform of any particular military organisation?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: For so far we saw, the 15 were dressed in HVO uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you're a military man and you were a military man at the time it. Can you describe the attitude of the soldiers that were accompanying him, the ones that you saw? What was their demeanour?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we got impression that they were deploying for a certain operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: They were armed, yes. Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall how they were armed, what sort of weapons they --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: What I remember is that they were armed with regular rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, in your report, then, you indicate that possibly they were intending to expel Muslim people from that part. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What makes you say that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Because they showed up there. So deploying means that -- that you are going to -- to execute an operation or an action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was there any ABiH military in that area? In other words, for --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. That had nothing to do with the confrontation line as well. It was in other area, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did this incident -- did you associate with any of the other activities that you'd been seeing in Mostar during your time up to that point?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, it fits, of course, in what we heard about operations by -- by special units. Small special units, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What types of operations are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Covert operations that normally took place at night. That was the reason also that probably he was very surprised to -- to see us at that moment. It had a reason, because we were stopped first on that day by the check-point, and after complaining by the officials we got approval to -- later on to go downtown.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you weren't supposed to be there.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Exactly. And -- and the information we got is that they normally operated in darkness, and after, let's say, the daylight hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I want to just be clear. What sort of operation are we talking about? You say they operated in darkness. What sort of operation?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We are talking about intimidation and ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. The next document I want to take you to is 3085. This will be a brief one, because now it's the 1st of July, sort of the first full day after the attack. And what was the situation in respect of your access or freedom of movement into Mostar, then, on this day?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, from -- from the 30th of June on we were not able to -- to enter Mostar any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then on page 2 of this report, 3085, it appears that you tried to arrange a meeting with Mr. Stojic, but you did not succeed to do that.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. The next exhibit is 3172. Now, is this one of your reports, Colonel, from the 4th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: ECMM M2 report?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And on this day, I want to direct you particularly now, on page 2, item 4, on the humanitarian activity. Given the fact that now you couldn't get access into Mostar, did you direct your attention and your activities in other areas, places where you could go?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. That -- that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, there's a reference in this section to a refugee camp in Capljina. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What do you recall about this trip to the refugee camp in Capljina?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: What I recall is that the people who were involved in preparing refugees to -- to transport or to send to Germany was -- were German relief helpers. I don't know -- I don't remember from what specific organisation they were, but I remember that they told us about their situation, and the people, the displaced persons and the refugees, were located in train wagons. That is what I remember very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Under -- under bad conditions, by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you were informed that these -- first of all, were these Muslim refugees or a different group?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were these Muslim refugees or were they of a different group?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Muslim. I think that most of them were Muslim refugees, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And there's a reference here to their being threatened almost every night by MP?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And turning the page, on the top part, so the of some complaints or some frustration perhaps about the international agencies now not having any freedom of movement. Was that the case? Was it frustrating to be there now without access to --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely, because there was a lot going on. The situation was more tense than it was before, of course. There was a reaction on the west side, and we couldn't go there to monitor. So that was, of course, a kind of frustration.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And there's a reference here to your inability to actually make contact now with any of the HVO people that you used to talk to.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Definitely. So it was -- it had to do with our overall freedom of movement to go from west to the east bank as we usually did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And finally toward the bottom there is a reference to "Muslim refugees systematically threatened in some communities of southern area of responsibility." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall about that, the situation with Muslims in -- in places like Capljina now after the attack?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. That is related to that visit, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Exhibit P 3184. Is this one of your reports, lieutenant -- Colonel, pardon me, dated the 5th of July, which is now the next day, the following day?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this memorandum, this report describes a meeting that you had in the evening with Bruno Stojic finally.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you did in fact -- or you did succeed to have a meeting with him to discuss the situation?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I don't intend to go through all of these points with you. You appear to have divided your report up into his treatment of political activity, which is in number 2 --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- and then secondly military activity on the following page, which is in paragraph 3. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now -- and he gave you information, again on page 1, concerning the political situation, about negotiations, his view that the time had been lost in negotiations and he goes on really about the situation and it's there for everyone to read.
