And he's complaining about or suggesting that the Spanish Battalion was providing arms to the armija, or that at least armija were in possession of arms from Spanish Battalion. And then ending with: "The limited freedom of movement in the combat zone is only necessary for the safety of international agencies, and that's not going to change." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. So did you have -- well, on the freedom of movement, did you raise this with him about trying to restore your freedom of movement within Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, for sure we did, but the problem here was they closed the road for us, and they justified that -- and he did it as well, and we do that because for your own safety. It's for your own safety that we don't let you go downtown Mostar. Well, it had nothing to do with our own safety because we were responsible, according to the ECMM instructions, for our own safety, and that's why we had an armoured car, and we were able to visit under difficult circumstances and dangerous circumstances the west and the east bank before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then continuing on, he's describing various points on the military side in paragraph 3 that the HVO barracks had been conquered. It's not reconquered by the HVO because it is not of special operational interest. And again he continues, bottom of the page about exact information that the armija wants to attack certain areas which continue, and he continues to describe what he believes are objectives of the armija. You know, taking all this together, both the political and the military information that he's providing and discussing with you, did it appear to you that Mr. Stojic was well-informed or not well-informed of the situation, at least, in the immediate Mostar area?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I think that he was well-informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Continuing down, item 4 relates to humanitarian activity. And you say here you've got a reliable source, it's unconfirmed, but again your interpreter has -- has said that between the 30th of June and now about 5.000 Muslim men were arrested on the west bank and transported to the barracks near the Heliodrom. And then there's another statement here attributed to your interpreter that at the same time about 400 Muslim families, without men, were expelled from the west to the east bank. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you comment with -- did you observe whether there was any, and maybe you can't because you weren't in Mostar, the general effect of the armija offensive on the humanitarian situation for Muslims in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, as I said, in the beginning it -- it seemed to be -- to give some relief about the very bad operation, and -- but at the same time, after -- after the attack it became more tense because there was more fighting continuing from both sides, and it affected actually the whole environment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was your impression --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: By the way, on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to move on, then, to the next exhibit, which is P 3181, which actually goes back. You have to go back to that one. Now, this report, your report that we just finished talking about is dated July 5th.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this document, 3184 [sic], first of all, have you ever seen this before other than when I showed it to you the other day?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Are you talking about 3181?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: 3181, yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes, but you said 3184.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: 3181, I never saw before, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Starting on the third page and working forward, first of all, what's the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: The date is the 5th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So it's the same date as your report talking about expulsion?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the third page originating from the Zahum local commune government commissioner contains a list of families whose members are in balija units. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what balija -- does that word mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Then there's a list of names continuing down, and then a remark that the Kavazbasic street has not been cleansed of Muslims. Another remark about balijas hiding in a garage. And then finally a raid in the evening or raid in the evening, signed by this government commissioner. You see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the immediate preceding page, and this is dated 5th of July, this is from the president of the Mostar municipality of the HVO government, a Dr. Stojan Vrlic -- Vrlic. He appears to be transmitting this list to Chief Bruno Stojic personally. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Subject being families of members of balija units. We are sending you enclosed the list of families from the Zahum local commune whose members are in balija units. Okay?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then finally on the top a sheet indicating the subject is notification from the Mostar municipality HVO government relating to families of members of balija. And the translation indicates that's a derogatory term for Muslim units. You see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, my question to you is this: In that this appears to relate to cleansing of Muslims, raiding Muslims in the evening and identifying their locations, is this consistent with ultimately the views you reached about the level of involvement of the HVO organisation in this eviction of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes, indeed it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is this consistent with the statements made to you by Mr. Stojic and the others that in fact it was an activity that was just being carried out by criminals?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is entirely speculative. This witness has never seen the document before. He has no idea of the accuracy of its content or what it concerns or anything else. He even was not -- says he's not familiar with the term balija. So for Mr. Scott to construct -- for Mr. Stringer to construct this elaborate speculative theory based on this document is entirely improper and argumentative, and I think Mr. Stringer is aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may respond, it's a practice that the Trial Chamber has approved and I think has approved numerous times. It's not been represented that the witness originated this document or that he saw it before, but he's clearly entitled to comment on it, particularly in light of the testimony he's given about his own meetings with Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question was whether it was consistent with the activity being carried out by criminals. He has no way of knowing, based on this document, whether the activity was carried out by criminals or anybody else. That's the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I've heard this differently, Mr. Murphy. I've heard the question saying is it consistent with what has been alleged with regard to criminals. So someone else has said so according to the Prosecutor. I did not hear the Prosecutor actually affirm that actions had been carried out by criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: That's exactly right, Your Honour, but the point is he's obviously trying to establish by this that -- that what he was told or says he was told by Mr. Stojic was inaccurate, and this document provides no basis for that. Your Honour is entirely right, but I think my point stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would agree it is for the Chamber to evaluate whether it is a contrast or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, it is for the Chamber to evaluate. My concern is we have really sat here this afternoon and had, I say with great respect, pretty much nothing from this witness except speculation and hearsay. And it really is reaching the point -- I know these things are technically -- hearsay is technically admissible in this Tribunal but it reaches a point really where it becomes an abuse of process to allow a witness sit here for hours and simply speculate without factual background. So I draw that to the Trial Chamber's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the witness has been spending the last two and a half hours commenting on reports he made at the time of the events. He's available for cross-examination on the very points he has written in the reports that he wrote at the time of the events in question. Moreover, he's testified before this Trial Chamber about specific meetings he's had with Mr. Murphy's client and the statements made to the witness by the client. So I dare say that is a far cry from hearsay and speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, it's a point of clarification, Your Honours, and it has to do with the translation of this particular document. Where it says "balija" throughout the document, it's in quotation marks. We have it italicised here, but it's in quotation marks. And also -- and it could be that's because that was the name of the unit or that's what the unit called themselves. And also, on the third page, Your Honours, and I believe you may recall, this was before Mr. Stringer came into the picture, there was some commenting about a unit called Balija, but on page 3 where under remarks it says number 1, "Cleansed of Muslims," again on the translation in the original language is cleansed of "balijas." So I mention that -- it's in the original. I mention that because Mr. Stringer obviously knows what the term means and the translator has pointed out that this is a derogatory term, but it may be that Mr. Stringer is -- is mistaken at least because of the quotation marks and the prior testimony we have heard, but that is something of course we would need to clarify at some point, but I raise that as a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say the following: Today the witness, when mentioning the context, did not specify the names of the streets or the persons involved when he describes events at night, but what he kept stressing and what the Prosecutor obtained from him in his replies was that these were families and civilians. When one looks at these documents carefully, one can see that only male names are listed. Along the names positions in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina are mentioned. And the last one under number 7 is a female name, and only the place where that person can be found is mentioned. And furthermore, when raids are mentioned in the last two points, it is stated very clearly that the raid was exclusively on a garage or a shelter where they would be hiding. The witness mentioned neither shelters nor raids nor garages so it might be a good idea for the Prosecutor to ask him whether he knows where these streets are, whether he has heard of the garage and the shelter and where they are in Mostar, and then we will know whether the witness can speak about this document or not. And it is my opinion that he can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, very briefly. Could the Prosecutor show us the first page of this document. He has shown the witness the document and the witness has said he has never seen the document. So it might be interesting to ask what this first page means, especially in view of the fact that twice the Prosecutor asked whether the document was dated the 12th of July, so that might be interesting to check. And it's especially interesting to see the front page, because I think it's important to ask the witness whether he knows what the front page means. The front page means that this is a file held by the Security Information Service which was checking this information. It's the cover of the file in fact. So it might be good to start from the first page, the front page rather than the third page, because this is causing confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the document that has been submitted to you by the Prosecution is a letter sent by the president of the municipality of Mostar, Dr. Stojan Vrlic, addressed apparently to Mr. Stojic personally. This document is dated the 5th of July, 1993. It was received, according to the stamp, on the 12th of July, 1993, by the defence department. Apparently the document arrived at the offices of the defence department. And on the first page the title is: "Families whose members are in balija units." And it is indicated, "We are sending the list of families from Zahum, families whose members are in balija units." We have a list of seven names among which 4, 5, 6 and 7 are apparently members of the ABiH, mainly members of the police, either the MUP, Ministry of the Interior, or -- or other members, other units of the BH, as well as, well, number 6 there is nothing specified. As for 1, 2, and 3, we don't have any idea who those people are. There are addresses as well, numbers that would seem to correspond to those places where those people lived. Now, when you had a conversation either with your interpreter or people whom you met in the street or the various people with whom you had discussions, did you find out that members of the ABiH might have been expelled or evicted from their apartments? Because that is what seems to be alleged by this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean one of the seven members?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not specifically these seven people whom you don't know, but were you told that in general members of the ABiH were evicted from their apartments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. That -- that was told before. But as I explained, it happened at night. So we never had proof of that operating by daytime in Mostar downtown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the content of that document, does it confirm what you had learned from your sources, or does this document, according to you, is it inconsistent or does it not have any substance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think it could be that it makes clear that it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Well, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just for clarification about what happened, again you mentioned the night-time being the time -- going back to the list itself, at the bottom it's indicated, "raid in the evening". Do you see that? Under remark number 2, "raid in the evening". Colonel, I'm sorry, I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: "Raid in the evening", is that consistent with --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, that means --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Raid in the evening, is that consistent with the information that you had been obtaining, that was coming to you previously?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Raid in the evening could -- could mean an operation by night, yeah, or in the evening. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And then remark number 1 about a particular street that has not been cleansed of Muslims. Again, is that consistent with what you were hearing previously about these sorts of activities?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Could be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, that's the part where I indicated that under the original language, it's "balijas," and there maybe a vast difference if we're talking about a unit with that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I mean, the translation I've got doesn't even use the word "balija" in that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I've indicated to Mr. Stringer, out of profession courtesy, to look at his original document. We have looked at it. Now it's obvious you don't need to be a B/C/S speaker, and I'm just shocked that he's applying these sorts of tactics.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I don't understand the point, Mr. President. I've got a translation in front of me. That's all I can work with. I don't think any of us who aren't native speakers of the original language are in a position to sort this out now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kovacic. He may be able to enlighten us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that I could be of assistance. We had this same discussion, and it was on the 17th of April. We had that same document and had this discussion. Now you have to look at the original document. Quite obviously, it is the name of a unit and that is something we've been claiming from day one and that is clear to all of us and it is in that context that you must interpret the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Defence counsel says that in fact the reference here is to units, and the Prosecution maintains that the term means Muslim. Well, it will be up to the Trial Chamber to decide. Please pursue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think we can move from this document now, Colonel, and I'm going to direct you now to Exhibit 3369. I have only two more to go, Mr. President. So we'll be able to finish with no difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by way of clarification, when the word "balija" is written with a small letter, then sometimes it is a derogatory term for Muslims, but in the Croatian language when you place a capital letter for Balija, then it is the name of a unit. So those are the differences. And they're quite clear. They're grammatical ones and quite clearly interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have the B/C/S version. We can put it on the ELMO so we can all see it. Otherwise, we can tender this at some point. But we expect the Prosecution to -- you know, to look at these matters and to correct them if they're not corrected. And -- but it's right here. It's very obvious. You can see it with the naked eye. You don't need to be a B/C/S speaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Stringer, Mr. Praljak has distinguished between balija with a "B" that is not a capital letter and balija with a capital "B", which would mean that it's a unit, capital "B" and quotation marks. So that's what Mr. Praljak says. So -- well, perhaps you can look into it further, explore the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We will look into it. I note that the document refers several times to units in the plural, and I think it's unlikely that you'd have multiple units given the same name, but again, none of us can sort it out at this point, and I am in a position to complete my direct examination today if we can -- if we can move beyond this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would prefer putting this on the ELMO, because again I hear Mr. Stringer saying two different things. Maybe he should ask the gentleman if he had heard of this particular unit. But it's crystal clear. Let's put it on the ELMO and let's get this over with.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I suggest at that counsel can do that during his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, during the cross-examination. Mr. Stringer, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Colonel, now I wanted to refer you to Exhibit P 3369. Do you have that one?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And this is -- is this your report dated the 10th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Just two points on this. On the bottom -- toward the bottom of page 1, in point number 6, you reference a visit with or to the Spanish Battalion the previous day, and you're writing information that you obtained during the course of that visit. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. There's a reference to Muslim males between the ages of 17 and 70 years old living in the area of Mostar and beyond border with Croatia that have been arrested. Most of them are in the Heliodrom. About 5 to 6.000. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. That's information that you received from the Spanish Battalion on this day?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And that number of 5.000 Muslim men arrested, is that consistent with the figure that was given to you previously by your interpreter, that was contained in the other report?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this refers to cleansing done in Dubrava, Stolac, Capljina, those areas; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now were those areas outside of your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you don't have personal knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: There's also -- you're reporting here that the HVO was divided politically into hard and soft liners. Again this was information provided to you by the Spanish Battalion; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I just wanted to make what clear. Do you necessarily share the assessment of the Spanish Battalion on this?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I do for Mr. Stojic, Maric, and I did agree with Puljic, because according to our observations and -- and -- the times that we talked to him, he belongs in the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: With the Hawks.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then just for the record, the others that you have not commented on are ones that you don't have an opinion on?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. The next exhibit is --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: By the way, may I explain this? In --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, in this document you distinguish between the Hawks and the Doves. Apparently among the Hawks were Mr. Stojic, Mr. Maric, Mr. Tomic, and Mr. Lasic, and then among the Doves would be Mr. Petkovic, Mr. Obradovic, and Mr. Puljic. Very well. But this difference that you mention, in fact it was something that was told to you by the Spanish Battalion. You didn't come to this distinction yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, but I just wanted to explain and that was the question by Mr. Stringer, that I -- when I -- when I would -- would put these gentlemen under whatever name, Hawks means in my interpretation nationalists. Okay? Strong nationalist. That is my interpretation of this when you ask me do you agree with this, this list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Doves in English would then -- are not nationalists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that strong. And I mean showing that to us in the conversations we had with them prior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just to clarify again because -- are there some people on that list that you don't -- you don't have an opinion because you didn't have sufficient contact to form an opinion?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. The people I didn't mention I don't have an opinion about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And just so the record's clear on that, I want to see if I can -- Stojic you had an opinion.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Stanko Maric; correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the opinion on those two is?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Strong nationalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Tomic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No opinion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Lasic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No opinion. Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you have really any dealings with General Petkovic --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- during that time? Obradovic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Also not in our area, as you see, so no opinion about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then finally Zlatko Puljic, who you've testified about.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was your opinion there?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I should name him as well a strong nationalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next exhibit, which is the final exhibit, Mr. President, is Exhibit 3900. And I should -- I should interject here. We're moving forward to the 2nd of August from the 10th of July, 1993, and during a period of about two weeks in the middle there did you actually leave Mostar and go on -- get a break outside the region?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I had a very short leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you then return from your break around the 3rd of July?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And by the end of July had freedom of movement and access to Mostar for you and ECMM been restored, or was it still barred, the access?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It still -- there was still no -- no freedom of movement for ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So with that as the background, this document 3900, dated the 2nd of August, 1993, do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That is report made by the head of the coordination centre, Sir Martin Garrod.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. The head of the Mostar coordination centre?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir Martin Garrod. So he was your supervisor or superior at this time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Who made this memorandum?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: He, on his personal title.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And this is a memorandum about a meeting that was held with Jadranko Prlic on the 2nd of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I was team member and present at that meeting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And have you had a chance now to review this memorandum prior to your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And even though it's not written by you, would you characterise it as -- as accurate, or would you agree with the statements that are contained in it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It is accurate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Just a couple questions about this. First of all, going into this meeting with Dr. Prlic, you indicated earlier you made a list of questions or would make a list of questions. Do you recall what were the objectives or the topics that you and Sir Garrod wanted to discuss with Dr. Prlic at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We had a list with some more topics focused on -- on our work as team member, but as you see here, Sir Martin Garrod focused on the most important thing at that moment. That was, of course, getting back freedom of movement and get -- and make it possible that we can do our work downtown Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So jumping ahead to page 2, item (f), there is a reference there as to the freedom of movement question. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That was one of the items that you wanted to discuss with him.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know why it was arranged to have a meeting with Dr. Prlic to discuss freedom of movement? Were you involved in arranging or organising the meeting at all?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We did by the HVO officials, yeah, but we only could do that by telephone, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the first page of this it's reporting a lot of things said by Mr. Prlic, Dr. Prlic, about events happening in other areas. I'll direct you to section (b) about Croats driven away from Bugojno, places Kakanj, Gornji Vakuf. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Skipping down, there was -- I believe, yes, in paragraph (d), an example of the Croats from Vares. So again, all of those places he's talking about the events, were these within your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Were these developments in areas within the area of responsibility of Sir Garrod?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So is it particularly helpful for you to be discussing the events in -- in these other locations?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. Whether it was helpful to him or not is irrelevant. What's relevant is that Dr. Prlic is pointing out at this meeting what is happening in Central Bosnia, and this gentleman being an EC monitor should have known about the events, and if he didn't, shame on him. But he was pointing out the events because everything was inter-related, and you have to look at the document in its whole, in its entirety, not cherry-picking as Mr. Stringer is doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is for cross-examination or closing argument. This isn't an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The question is this -- I'll restate it. Discusses of events in Bugojno and elsewhere, was it -- was it helpful to you in gaining what you were seeking, which, again, was freedom of movement through -- in your local area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the second page there is a discussion in paragraph (e) about whether there would be separate republics, what Dr. Prlic's views were on that, and I just want, again based on your focus of your area of responsibility, there's a statement that's attributed to him in here in which he states: "His first principle was that people should be able to live where they wanted to live and stay where they wished to stay." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, my question is whether, based on your experience in Mostar, was that actually taking place?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Because this is a statement that was not shared by everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was everybody in Mostar able to live and stay where they wanted?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Moving down to section (g), you then raised, as you've indicated, the question of freedom of movement, and there's discussion about that, and then subsequently in -- at the bottom of the page a reference to possible exchange of prisoners, and then actually that's also referred to in paragraph (h). So those two issues, freedom of movement and possible exchange of prisoners. Do you recall those two topics being discussed here?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether there was any resolution or progress made on those points either during the meeting or during your time, your remaining time in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, my remaining time in Mostar didn't show freedom of movement, and the exchange of prisoners was an important hot item but not in my time frame. It didn't happen in my time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again just to complete that, he has indicated in paragraph (g) here that freedom of movement relates to the HVO military, and then secondly he's indicated that he would speak to Stojic and Bosic favourably on that period. Do you know whether that ever happened?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. Stringer, you finished your examination-in-chief, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. We resume tomorrow at 2.15. We will resume with the cross-examination, and it will continue until Thursday, because tomorrow is Wednesday. Sir, as you know, you made a solemn declaration at the beginning of your testimony which means that you cannot meet with anyone until tomorrow neither from Prosecution nor from Defence. I wanted to say this. So we'll meet again tomorrow at 2.15 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 11th day of July, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
